title: Dispatch: context-packet intervention seam (attempt 1)
description:

sections 12.3, 13.1, 13.3). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, and
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`.

from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12` AFTER dispatches 1 and 2 merged into it. Dependencies

This is the dispatch that actually changes what the DM receives. Everything it
depends on already exists on your base branch:

- `packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts` —
  `renderContextPacketMessage(trace): RenderedContextPacket` (dispatch 1). Read

- `packages/core/src/discovery/measurements.ts` — `measureAcceptedStateEffect`,

- `packages/core/src/discovery/shadow.ts` — schema `discovery-shadow-v2`, its

Verify each of those exists on your branch before you start. If one is missing,

## Code survey (read before writing)

- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts:163-171` — the
  `recordDiscoveryShadow` dep and its doc comment; `:806-838` — the Phase 2 seam
  between `assembleContext` and `renderContextMessage`, where `baseUserMessage`
  is computed; `:1140-1183` — where `retrievedContext` is recorded and the
  evidence is completed and written.
- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts:982` —
  `renderContextMessage`: the sections and their joining (`\n\n`).
- `packages/core/src/model/client.ts:158-182` — `ModelCompleteInput`. This is
  the ADR 0010 provider-neutral seam: `messages` is what every adapter family
  receives identically.
- `docs/adr/0010-api-native-vs-agent-harness-model-adapter-seam.md` — read
  decisions 1 and 2. "Provider-neutral" in this bead means the packet reaches
  the model through the shared `ModelClient` surface, never through one
  provider's agent loop, system-prompt shaping, or MCP channel.
- `packages/core/test/discovery/shadowRuntime.test.ts` — `RUNTIME_REACH` (the
  pinned per-probe M1/M2 table), the byte-identity parity test, the per-execution
  probe loop at `:489`, `ScriptedModel`, `StructuredScriptedModel`,
  `ScriptedAuditor`, and the support installers.
- `packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryBoundary.test.ts` — `SHADOW_SEAM_FILE`
  and `SHADOW_SEAM_MODULES`. The orchestrator may import from discovery ONLY
  `../discovery/shadow.js` and `../discovery/types.js`. Do not widen this list.
  Route the renderer through `shadow.js`.
- `packages/core/src/memory/turnTrace.ts:55-65` — the `discoveryShadow` column
  comment, which currently states that nothing in the column reached the DM.

## Deliverable 1 — the mode, as a union

Replace `RunTurnDeps.recordDiscoveryShadow?: boolean` with

```ts
discoveryMode?: 'off' | 'shadow' | 'intervene';   // default 'off'
```

and update every caller and test. Two booleans would make
`{shadow: false, intervene: true}` representable and meaningless; this codebase
consistently prefers a union that makes an impossible state unrepresentable, and
the three states really are exclusive. `'off'` runs no discovery at all.
`'shadow'` keeps W9's contract exactly: discovery observes, records, and
injects nothing, and the DM message stays byte-identical with `'off'`.
`'intervene'` observes, records, AND injects.

Write the doc comment to say that `'intervene'` is the first mode in which the
DM's input differs, that it is an experiment and not part of released play, and
that packet presence is never evidence the model used the material (§12.3).

## Deliverable 2 — the intervention entry point, inside `shadow.ts`

The orchestrator must not gain a new discovery import. Add to `shadow.ts`:

```ts
export interface DiscoveryInterventionCapture {
  readonly capture: DiscoveryShadowCapture;
  /** Absent when the capture failed, so nothing can be injected. */
  readonly rendered?: RenderedContextPacket;
}
export function captureDiscoveryIntervention(
  input: ShadowDiscoveryInput,
): DiscoveryInterventionCapture;
```

It runs the SAME capture path as `captureDiscoveryShadow` and then renders the
packet. It must be as total and failure-tolerant as the shadow capture is: a
render failure is recorded as a capture failure and injects nothing, and never
propagates into the turn. An observation point that can abort a player's turn is
worse than no observation point — that reasoning is already in `shadow.ts`'s
header and applies with more force once the packet is load-bearing.

To render, `captureDiscoveryIntervention` needs the LIVE `DiscoveryTrace`, not
the projection. Restructure the shared capture so both entry points build the
live trace once and project it once; do not run discovery twice, and do not
render from the projection.

## Deliverable 3 — injection, through the shared model seam

In `orchestrator.ts`, when the mode is `'intervene'` and a rendered packet
exists, the DM's user message becomes the base message plus the rendered packet
appended as a further section, joined exactly as `renderContextMessage` joins
its own sections (`\n\n`).

Three hard requirements:

1. **Additive, never rewriting.** The base message must survive as an exact
   prefix of the injected message. Discovery does not edit, reorder, or filter
   what the context assembler produced.
2. **One message, one seam.** Injection happens by composing the string handed
   to `ModelCompleteInput.messages`. Do NOT put it in `system`, do NOT change
   the tool definitions, do NOT touch `buildSystemPrompt`, and do NOT add a
   provider-conditional branch anywhere.
3. **The trace records what was actually sent.** `retrievedContext` at
   `:1145` currently re-calls `renderContextMessage(assembled)`, which would
   record the base message while the DM received the injected one. Record the
   message that was actually sent. This also means the injected text is durably
   recorded exactly once — do not store a second copy in the discovery
   evidence.

## Deliverable 4 — the delivery record, extending v2

Dispatch 2 introduced `discovery-shadow-v2`. Extend it; do NOT bump again.
Add a required field to `DiscoveryShadowEvidence`:

```ts
export type ShadowDelivery =
  | { readonly mode: 'observed'; readonly injected: false }
  | {
      readonly mode: 'intervened';
      readonly injected: true;
      readonly renderedBytes: number;
      /** SHA-256 of the rendered packet text, binding this evidence to the
       *  message recorded in `turn_trace.retrieved_context`. */
      readonly renderedSha256: string;
      readonly candidateCount: number;
      readonly mustConsiderOverflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[];
    }
  | { readonly mode: 'intervened'; readonly injected: false; readonly reason: string };

readonly delivery: ShadowDelivery;
```

The third arm is the honest one and is the reason this is a union rather than a
boolean plus optional fields: intervention was requested but the capture or the
render failed, so nothing was injected, and the reason is recorded. A reader
must never have to infer "did the DM actually get this?" from whether an
optional field happens to be present.

Extend the fail-closed reader to admit `delivery` and reject every malformed
arm, in the same declared-here-not-imported style the existing validator uses.

Update the `discoveryShadow` column comment in
`packages/core/src/memory/turnTrace.ts`: the claim that nothing in the column
reached the DM is no longer unconditionally true, and the comment must now point
at `delivery` as the field that says which it was.

## Deliverable 6 — keep W9's guarantees intact

`'shadow'` mode must remain byte-identical to `'off'`. The existing parity test
in `shadowRuntime.test.ts` proves that for the old boolean; port it to the mode
union and ADD the complementary assertion that `'intervene'` is NOT byte-
identical — a parity test that would pass in all three modes proves nothing
about the mode that matters.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape any existing test, and do not widen
  `SHADOW_SEAM_MODULES` in `discoveryBoundary.test.ts`.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or anything under `.claude/`.
- No ADR and no new design-document section is authorized here. If you believe
  the design is wrong, record it with
  `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.12.3 --append-notes` and file a follow-up with
  `bd create`.

## Scope boundary for this dispatch

You deliver the SEAM (deliverables 1-4 and 6). A sibling dispatch
(`eshyra-o9bd.19.12.4`) owns the intervention evidence suite
`packages/core/test/discovery/packetIntervention.test.ts` and runs after you.
Do not create that file.

You still owe evidence for the seam ITSELF, in the suites that already own
these surfaces:

S1. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — the ported parity test: `'shadow'` mode leaves the
    whole model input byte-identical with `'off'`, AND `'intervene'` does NOT.
    A parity test that passed in all three modes would prove nothing about the
    mode that matters.
S2. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — an intervention turn's model input contains the
    shadow turn's rendered context as an exact PREFIX, and the remainder is the
    rendered packet text. Injection is additive; it never rewrites what the
    context assembler produced.
S3. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — `turn_trace.retrieved_context` for an
    intervention turn equals the message the model actually received, not the
    base message. Recording the base message while the DM got the injected one
    would make the trace lie about the turn.
S4. `shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts` — the v2 reader admits each valid
    `delivery` arm and rejects every malformed one, including the shape that
    claims `mode: 'intervened'` with `injected: true` while omitting the
    rendered identity, and an `injected: false` intervened arm with no reason.
S5. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — a capture FAILURE under `'intervene'` injects
    nothing, records the third `delivery` arm with its reason, and does not
    fail the turn. An observation point that can abort a player's turn is worse
    than no observation point.

Report the observed test counts before and after against the base commit.

COMPLETED at commit be783a0 on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.12.3, base df0fa7f.

Delivered deliverables 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 (bead has no deliverable 5; the sibling
.12.4 owns the M1-M12 intervention evidence suite and is not touched here).

1. RunTurnDeps.recordDiscoveryShadow?: boolean replaced with
   discoveryMode?: 'off' | 'shadow' | 'intervene' (default 'off'). All
   callers/tests in shadowRuntime.test.ts, shadowCapabilityEvents.test.ts,
   shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts ported.

2. shadow.ts: captureRawShadow() is the shared try/catch that runs discovery
   ONCE and returns the LIVE DiscoveryTrace (or a failure). projectCapture()
   turns that into the existing DiscoveryShadowCapture (projected) shape.
   captureDiscoveryShadow is now a one-line wrapper. New
   captureDiscoveryIntervention runs the same raw capture, then renders from
   the live trace via renderContextPacketMessage; a render failure downgrades
   the WHOLE capture to a failure (new ShadowFailure stage 'render') rather
   than leaving `rendered` absent beside a trace-bearing capture, so
   DiscoveryInterventionCapture's "rendered absent iff capture failed"
   invariant holds structurally, not just by convention.

3. orchestrator.ts: capture happens once, right after assembleContext, before
   buildSystemPrompt. 'intervene' mode appends
   `\n\n${renderedContextPacketMessage.text}` to the base rendered context
   (same join renderContextMessage uses internally) to form baseUserMessage,
   which every retry/correctiveNote attempt is built from -- additive only,
   base message is always an exact prefix. turn_trace.retrieved_context now
   records baseUserMessage (what was actually sent), not a fresh
   renderContextMessage(assembled) re-render. No system-prompt, tool-schema,
   or provider-conditional touch.

4. discovery-shadow-v2 extended (not re-bumped) with a required `delivery:
   ShadowDelivery` field: {mode:'observed', injected:false} | {mode:
   'intervened', injected:true, renderedBytes, renderedSha256, candidateCount,
   mustConsiderOverflow} | {mode:'intervened', injected:false, reason}.
   renderedSha256 = sha256 of the exact text appended (computed in
   orchestrator.ts from the same RenderedContextPacket used for injection, not
   recomputed independently). Fail-closed reader (checkDelivery +
   checkRetentionOverflow) admits each arm with exactKeys, plus a cross-check
   against the row's own trace/failure (injected:true requires a trace present,
   injected:false under 'intervened' requires a recorded failure) -- this
   cross-check was not explicitly asked for in S4 but protects a genuine
   impossible state the same way the existing trace/failure-exclusivity check
   does; flagging in case that's considered scope creep.
   turnTrace.ts's discoveryShadow column comment updated: "nothing reached the
   DM" is no longer unconditionally true; points at `delivery` as the field
   that says which.

6. Ported the W9 byte-identity parity test (shadowRuntime.test.ts) to the mode
   union and added the complementary assertion that 'intervene' is NOT
   byte-identical with 'off'.
